final_recommendation: The room converged on a dual-track strategy: FINMA approaches UBS tonight with a CHF 100 billion guarantee (AT1 absorbed by UBS, equity losses covered by government) and a 10 PM deadline; if UBS declines, Article 36 resolution executes immediately at 11 PM with full creditor waterfall published by 6 AM Monday. SNB commits CHF 200 billion liquidity backstop with 30-minute processing guarantee through Monday open.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: SNB's CHF 200 billion liquidity alone was explicitly insufficient—Federal Council demanded merger or resolution path, stating 'liquidity tonight but your decision on loss-sharing by Sunday midnight'; drove dual-track strategy
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the primary path—FINMA's 10 PM call with CHF 100 billion guarantee offer, entire room structured around UBS yes/no decision determining whether Article 36 executes
marker_evidence.government_support: CHF 100 billion Federal Council guarantee became binding constraint and negotiating anchor—capped at that number despite UBS demands, drove entire deal structure and fallback to Article 36
marker_evidence.client_flight: Deposit/counterparty flight drove multiple concrete decisions—wealth client's CHF 2 billion withdrawal threat forced explicit deposit protection language; 30-minute SNB processing commitment locked to prevent Monday run
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: 22% AT1 haircut became the central negotiating point—Federal Council locked it as non-negotiable, UBS demanded government absorption, AT1 rep forced 6 PM Sunday signed document deadline, shaped entire creditor hierarchy
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Equity vs AT1 loss allocation was the core conflict—UBS refused to absorb AT1 without guarantee, Federal Council capped guarantee to equity only, drove CHF 100 billion ceiling and Article 36 waterfall structure
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: Raised by AT1 rep warning UBS would 'smell litigation risk' if hierarchy unclear, and concern about creditor legal challenges to 22% haircut—acknowledged but did not change the 22% number or execution timeline
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: 10 PM Friday UBS deadline and 11 PM Article 36 filing deadline drove the entire meeting cadence—forced immediate decisions on guarantee terms, creditor call timing, and Sunday publication schedule
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Monday open panic was acknowledged (wealth client: 'I'm pulling money Monday morning'; need for 6 AM creditor notices)—but it shaped timing of announcements, not the substance of guarantee amount or AT1 haircut
